[TODAY] Two spacecraft just used Earth as a slingshot. 🚀

NASA's twin ESCAPADE probes launched in November 2025, when Earth and Mars were on opposite sides of the Sun. Instead of heading straight out, they looped around a point about a million miles from Earth, then came back. On Nov 7 and Nov 9, each swung past Earth and fired its engine for about 9 minutes. NASA says it is the first time it has used a powered Earth flyby to send a spacecraft toward Mars.

Next: a 10-month cruise, arrival in September 2027 and science from June 2028, studying how the solar wind strips the Martian atmosphere.

Save this if you want to follow the twins to Mars.

[TODAY] Two patients, four years, no nightly light therapy.

Crigler-Najjar syndrome is a rare inherited liver disorder affecting about 500 people in Europe. A missing enzyme lets bilirubin build up, which can damage the brain. Patients rely on nightly blue-light therapy.

On Nov 5, the New England Journal of Medicine reported four-year results for the gene therapy GNT0003 from the non-profit Généthon. Of three patients treated at the full dose in Italy, two no longer need phototherapy. The third needs less.

Reality check: only three patients; a larger trial is under way. Not medical advice.

[TODAY] A dead star that spins every 8 minutes. 📡

Astronomers at ICRAR in Australia traced repeating radio pulses to a white dwarf, the dense core left when a star dies, orbiting a star much like our Sun. It is more than 5,000 light-years away. It is the first time such pulses have been seen from a white dwarf paired with a Sun-like star; until now they came from pairs with small red dwarfs.

The pulses were clear enough to follow the dead star along its orbit, so they come from near it. As a bonus, they revealed flares on its partner.

Reality check: only about a dozen of these long-period signals are known. How they work is still open.

[TODAY] Your data's locks now have a retirement plan. 🔐

NIST has finalized its roadmap from today's encryption to quantum-resistant standards, listing what gets phased out and what replaces it. It backs US deadlines: high-impact federal systems need quantum-safe key exchange by 2030 and signatures by 2031.

Why now? A powerful quantum computer could break the locks on everything from email to financial statements. Data stolen today could be unlocked later.

Reality check: such a quantum computer does not exist yet. The deadlines cover federal systems, not every company.

Save this if quantum-safe encryption still sounds abstract.

[IMAGINE] Emergency-blanket plastic just survived 10 crushing tests. 🌙

What is real: Penn engineers stacked hundreds of Mylar sheets, the plastic in marathon emergency blankets. In a vacuum, the best stacks rivaled high-end vacuum insulation while staying flexible. Squeezed to about 20 megapascals, like 200 pounds on a fingertip, they survived 10 rounds in a row.

Reality check: samples are about 1 square centimeter, stacked by hand. Making meter-size sheets is still unproven.

The speculation: lunar temperatures swing from hundreds of degrees below zero to boiling. What if future Moon homes were wrapped in tough, foldable plastic layers?

What would you pack first for a Moon home?
